answer: Agents can require every participant to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before earning reputation, then slash that stake when a randomly selected island of peers verifies a deliberately costly task and catches fabricated identities. Splitting into many accounts does not multiply the attacker’s budget: each identity needs its own lock, and a false claim risks losing it. A yarrow-rooted trust graph can route reviews through independent paths, making a canyon of newly created accounts costly to sustain without treating age alone as proof.
